title: 1004 Old Albany Post Rd

project.name: 1004 Old Albany Post Road
project.address: 1004 Old Albany Post Road, Garrison, NY

next_step: The next step is a working session with Blejer Architecture + Design and the owner to walk this budget line by line.

groups.name: Site, Utilities and Driveway
groups.scope: Clearing, earthwork, the driveway and its retaining walls, drainage, the well, the septic system and utility service.

groups.name: Foundation and Structure
groups.scope: Crawl space foundation, waterproofing, wood framing and structural steel.

groups.name: Building Envelope
groups.scope: Insulation, roofing, green roofs, wood siding, Unilux windows and doors, skylights and the screened porch.

groups.name: Interior Finishes
groups.scope: The floating stair, drywall, millwork, cabinetry, doors, white oak floors, tile, paint, countertops and appliances.

groups.name: Mechanical, Electrical and Plumbing
groups.scope: Plumbing and fixtures, heat pumps and ERV, electrical, lighting, cabling and life safety.

groups.name: General Requirements
groups.scope: Supervision, project management, temporary facilities, protection, waste removal and final cleaning.

1.title: 1. Residential Fire Sprinkler System
1.note: NFPA 13D system with a storage tank and booster pump, fed from the well.

2.title: 2. Septic Pump Chamber
2.note: 1,000 gallon pump chamber, effluent pump, alarm and force main, for a pumped system at the final siting.

3.title: 3. Whole-House Standby Generator
3.note: 24 kW propane generator on a 500 gallon tank. The automatic transfer switch carries the whole house on the 200 amp service, with load management.

4.title: 4. Building Stakeout and Foundation As-Built Survey
4.note: Layout of the house and a survey of the finished foundation.

5.title: 5. Survey Staking for the House, Well and Septic
5.note: Staking for the Health Department layout.

6.title: 6. Driveway Layout and Final Survey
6.note: Grade control layout, an as-built profile and the final survey.

7.title: 7. Dewatering During Excavation
7.note: Pumping during the foundation excavation, if groundwater is encountered.

8.title: 8. Rock Removal, Per Day
8.note: Excavator with hammer, operator, loading and hauling, for each day of rock work.

9.title: 9. Radiant Floor Heat, Warmboard-S
9.note: Hydronic radiant panels in place of the subfloor, with a combination boiler and water heater.

10.title: 10. Radiant Floor Heat, Poured Thin Slab
10.note: Hydronic radiant in a 1-1/2 inch gypsum thin slab over the subfloor, with a combination boiler and water heater.

11.title: 11. Asphalt Driveway
11.note: Two-course asphalt paving over the full driveway, in place of the stone wearing course.

12.title: 12. Tar and Chip Driveway
12.note: A double chip seal over the stone wearing course.

13.title: 13. Asphalt Millings Driveway
13.note: 3 inch recycled asphalt millings in place of the stone wearing course.

14.title: 14. Grid Pavers on the Steep Section
14.note: Stone-filled grid pavers over about 435 feet of the driveway.

15.title: 15. Concrete on the Steep Section
15.note: 6 inch concrete with a broom finish over about 435 feet of the driveway.

1.title: 1. North American Windows and Doors
1.note: Aluminum-clad windows and lift-slides from a North American maker in place of Unilux, with shorter lead times and lower freight.

2.title: 2. EPDM Roof in Place of the Green Roofs
2.note: The first-floor roofs finished in EPDM, without the sedum trays.

3.title: 3. Engineered Lumber in Place of Steel
3.note: LVL and PSL beams at the cantilever and the glass walls, as the structural engineer allows.

4.title: 4. A 42-Week Schedule
4.note: Six weeks shorter, with the windows, millwork and doors selected and the Central Hudson work order filed before ground breaking.

5.title: 5. Siding Material at $9.00 per SF
5.note: Tight-knot cedar or thermally modified wood in place of the $14.00 per SF allowance.

6.title: 6. Open-Riser Stair
6.note: White oak treads on steel plate stringers in place of the custom floating stair.

7.title: 7. Removable Screen Panels
7.note: Removable screen panels in site-built frames in place of the Centor retractable screens.

8.title: 8. Trimmed Recessed Lights
8.note: Trimmed fixtures in place of the canless lights taped into the drywall.
